newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale's CWB plans "very positive" - CWB chief.
newsitem.headline: Goodale's CWB plans "very positive" - CWB chief.

text.p: Canada's plans to revamp the way the Canadian Wheat Board is run and conducts its business are "very positive," CWB chief commissioner Lorne Hehn said.
"It's very positive. I think he's listened to the farmers and he's come down the middle," Hehn told Reuters.
Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale announced plans Friday to allow the CWB to make cash purchases of grain and change its corporate structure to a board of governors.
Prairie farmers may be polled on whether barley should remain within the CWB monopoly. The poll could take place this winter, Goodale said.
Hehn declined to speculate on how the Prairies' 110,000 farmers would vote if such a plebiscite were held.
"I think this issue has to be settled once and for all," Hehn said.
CWB monopoly opponents, however, predicted most farmers would favour an open market in barley exports.
"I'm confident we can win this vote to take barley out of the Board," Western Barley Growers Association president Wayne Kriz said.
Cash purchases should help the CWB source grain when spot markets move rapidly and outpace the agency's monthly forecast.
"It would help us source grain when the market is moving rapidly," Hehn said. "And it would help in times of high demurrage costs."
Demurrage is a penalty paid when vessels are delayed at export position. Delays may stem from transportation problems or supply shortfalls.
"Certainly, this package accomodates a lot of the changes we wanted," Hehn said.
